message.content:
In /home/user/lance-graph, read through .claude/board/EPIPHANIES.md, .claude/board/LATEST_STATE.md, and .claude/board/PR_ARC_INVENTORY.md and extract everything said about PRs #1019 through #1040 (inclusive). Report only what exists with exact file:line citations. Never invent or infer beyond what's written.

First, grep each of "#1019" through "#1040" (case-sensitive, word-bounded) across the three files and report hit counts, then read the substantive ones (skip any with 0 hits, just list them as zero).

For EACH PR number that has hits, report:
1. What the PR did (in the doc's own words/quotes where stated plainly)
2. Its status: SHIPPED / SUPERSEDED / REVERTED / IN-PROGRESS / DISPUTED / OPEN — read this from the doc's own language (⊘ markers, "SUPERSEDES", "WITHDRAWN", operator rulings, merge status, etc.)
3. Any measured numbers, test counts, or falsifier names explicitly tied to that PR
4. Any real defect found and fixed (a genuine "review caught X, fixed by Y" story) — this session specifically values self-correction/falsification episodes

Additionally, flag explicitly (with citation) if ANY of these PRs touch, in priority order:
- **Rubicon / Heckhausen / Libet / commitment-phase geometry** — HIGHEST PRIORITY. Specifically look for a file literally named `revision.rs` (search crates/lance-graph-planner/src and crates/lance-graph-supervisor/src for it if not already found), and for Libet timing bands like -550ms/-220ms/0 or similar three-phase pre-commit windows. Also flag anything in `lance-graph-planner` or `lance-graph-supervisor::kanban_actor` specifically (the user says these are the REAL homes of the Rubicon model, correcting an earlier finding that treated it as isolated to lance-graph-contract's rubicon_witness.rs/kanban.rs).
- R2IL, HHTL cascade/address geometry, CollapseGate/rung/superposition, the persist_sink/cycle_driver commit machinery (continuing from #879/#911/#912/#1000-1018), the 12-byte/96-bit facet register, BLASGraph/semiring, BPE/token/trie, p64-bridge/cognitive-shader-driver.

Output: one section per PR number with hits, each with the four items above (Rubicon-flagged PRs can run long, others keep to ~100-200 words). End with a one-paragraph connected-narrative overview if the documents themselves make one visible via direct cross-references between these PRs.

Use when the user provides a strand ID (bd-XXXX) and asks to investigate, scope, or understand the work needed.

Use when the user reports that the preview's appearance, spacing, classes, or DOM structure doesn't match the rendered site — phrases like "preview vs render differs", "preview shows X differently", "spacing/margin/padding off", "DOM doesn't match", "missing class in preview", or shows a specific computed-style mismatch (e.g. "17px in preview, 34px in render"). Also invoked explicitly via `/preview-parity`.

Use when the user asks for writing improvement, prose review, revision suggestions, help making writing clearer or more readable, feedback on a draft, or mentions clarity, flow, emphasis, sentence structure, or "why this passage is hard to read". - upgrade-cargo-deps: Survey the workspace for available Rust dependency upgrades, apply patch/minor bumps in an isolated worktree, run full `cargo xtask verify`, and produce a plan doc + per-major braid strands so the user can review and merge. The strict sequencing is the anti-mush protocol. Canonical harness spec: .claude/agents/5plus3-council.md.

Good for UI mockups and screen flows, landing pages, marketing and social graphics, and print pieces — posters, flyers, brochures as single-page artboards; memos and reports as one flowing artboard. Use when someone wants a design, mockup, wireframe, UI or screen design, landing page, poster, flyer, brochure, banner, card, one-pager, or any visual layout they would rather tweak by hand than in code. Only for CREATING or re-seeding a canvas; an existing one is edited in its published Artifact.

Teaches a design-system-agnostic method: a form heuristic, a color formula with a runnable validator, mark specs, and interaction rules. done
